# This folder is a product backlog

A note here is a work item when it names one of the types below, or carries the parent property — naming one, or left empty to say it is a root, and the folder does not make it one. The other properties do not enrol it: a note carrying only an order or a state is still an ordinary note. Nor is the question asked one note at a time — a note that holds a work item is kept with it, so an untyped page grouping typed ones stays. The hierarchy between the items lives in frontmatter rather than in folders, on purpose. They stay plain markdown, so they can be read, written and reviewed in any editor, with or without Obsidian and the Product Backlog view that generated this file.

This document is generated from that view's configuration, so the property names below are the ones this backlog actually uses.

## The item types

Epic → Feature → PBI → Task is a ladder: each level holds the next one down. Issue, Bug, Idea and Deliverable sit *beside* it — they hang from any rung above the deepest and hold `Task` items wherever they hang, which is why they are types rather than levels. Milestone and Iteration are neither: a marker hangs from nothing and holds nothing, and states a date rather than work. Test suite → Test case is a **second ladder**, for tests rather than for work: a `Test suite` hangs from nothing, and the two ladders share only `Task`, the rung at the bottom of each.

| Type | Parent may be | Children may be |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Epic` | *(nothing — it is a root)* | `Feature`, `Issue`, `Bug`, `Idea`, `Deliverable` |
| `Feature` | *(nothing — it is a root)*, `Epic` | `PBI`, `Issue`, `Bug`, `Idea`, `Deliverable` |
| `PBI` | *(nothing — it is a root)*, `Feature` | `Task`, `Issue`, `Bug`, `Idea`, `Deliverable` |
| `Task` | *(nothing — it is a root)*, `PBI`, `Task`, `Issue`, `Bug`, `Idea`, `Deliverable`, `Test case` | `Task` |
| `Issue` | *(nothing — it is a root)*, `Epic`, `Feature`, `PBI` | `Task` |
| `Bug` | *(nothing — it is a root)*, `Epic`, `Feature`, `PBI` | `Task` |
| `Idea` | *(nothing — it is a root)*, `Epic`, `Feature`, `PBI` | `Task` |
| `Deliverable` | *(nothing — it is a root)*, `Epic`, `Feature`, `PBI` | `Task` |
| `Milestone` | *(nothing — it is a root)* | *(nothing)* |
| `Iteration` | *(nothing — it is a root)* | *(nothing)* |
| `Test suite` | *(nothing — it is a root)* | `Test case` |
| `Test case` | *(nothing — it is a root)*, `Test suite` | `Task` |

Write the type exactly as spelled above; matching is case-insensitive but the spelling is the vocabulary. A type this plugin does not ship is kept as written and shown as itself. Nothing rewrites it into one of these.

## The properties that carry the hierarchy

These are the keys **this** backlog uses. They are configurable per view, so they are read out of the configuration rather than assumed.

| Property | On | Holds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `parent` | Every item except a root | A link to the parent note: `"[[Note name]]"`. Quote it, or YAML reads the brackets as a list. Present but empty means the top level |
| `order` | Anything you want ranked | A number. The rank among the notes sharing a parent — see below. Without one an item sorts after the ranked ones |
| `type` | Anything you want typed | One of the type names above, or one of your own. Without one an item takes the level its position implies |
| `tags` | Optional | Tags, as a YAML list or one string |

The parent link is read generously: `"[[Note name]]"`, a bare note name, an alias (`"[[Note name|what it reads as]]"`) and a YAML list whose first entry is any of those all resolve to the same note. A link that resolves to nothing leaves the item where it is rather than dropping it. Numbers may be written as strings.

A key with **no value** — `parent:` and nothing after it — reads as the top level, which is what this plugin writes when it moves something there. Omitting the key entirely means the same thing here.

A **type of your own** is kept and shown, but it does not enrol a note that has no parent: only the types listed above are evidence on their own. Give such a note a parent, or it stays out of the tree.

## Ranking

`order` ranks an item among the notes that share its parent — lowest first. Nothing is global: the same number under two different parents is two unrelated ranks. The view writes them 10 apart, leaving room to insert without renumbering, and renumbers a group only when a move needs it.

Two siblings may end up sharing a number, and an item may carry none at all. Nothing breaks: the tie is settled by the order the base itself returned them in — whatever sort is configured in the Bases toolbar, file name by default — and items without a number sort last. That means the tie-break is a view setting rather than a property of these notes, so give siblings distinct numbers when writing by hand.

## Where notes are filed

Folders are filing, not hierarchy: the tree comes from the properties above, so a note is in the right place wherever it lives. What follows is only where **this** view puts a note it creates, in this order:

1. The folder configured for the type, when it has one.
2. The home folder, `docs`.
3. Wherever most of the existing items already live.

| Type | Folder |
| --- | --- |
| `Epic` | `docs/requirements` |
| `Feature` | `docs/requirements` |
| `PBI` | `docs/requirements` |
| `Task` | `docs/tasks` |
| `Issue` | `docs/issues` |
| `Bug` | `docs/bugs` |
| `Idea` | `docs/ideas` |
| `Deliverable` | `docs/deliverables` |
| `Milestone` | `docs/milestones` |
| `Iteration` | `docs/iterations` |
| `Test suite` | `docs/tests/suites` |
| `Test case` | `docs/tests/cases` |

## A note, written by hand

A `PBI` under a `Feature` called *Checkout redesign*, ranked 20 — after every sibling ranked below that and before every sibling above it, which is all a number here ever means. Nothing else is needed: the view fills in what it writes itself.

```markdown
---
type: PBI
parent: "[[Checkout redesign]]"
order: 20
---

# Pay with a saved card

Whatever the note is about.
```

## What the view will and will not do to these notes

- **The type rules are advisory.** They decide what the view *offers*; nothing is refused for the type a move would give a note, and a type you declare is the type you keep: a `Task` under an `Epic` stays one, at its own level, however oddly it sits. Only a note with **no** type takes the level its position implies, and a type this plugin does not ship sits one rung below its parent so its own children continue the ladder. The one move the view withholds for a **type** reason is a move between the two ladders above, and only for the two notes that read their ladder from where they hang: a `Task`, the rung both ladders share, and a note with no `type` at all. Either would change ladder by being moved, and the row would leave the screen it was moved on, so the move is not offered. Every other type keeps its ladder wherever it lands. Moving a note never rewrites its type.
- **Only the properties above are written.** Prose, headings and any other frontmatter are left alone.
- **Levels, progress and board position are derived, never stored.** Do not write them back: they are computed from the properties above every time the view opens.
- **A note nothing links to is still a note.** An unresolved parent leaves the item at the top level rather than hiding it.
